lead.t: | Acute hemolytic transfusion reaction (AHTR) | Fever, flank pain, dark urine, hypotension, rapid fall in Hb, positive direct Coombs | Immediate onset, evidence of intravascular hemolysis, complement‑mediated, not primarily respiratory. |

snip.t: | Acute hemolytic transfusion reaction (AHTR) | Fever, flank pain, dark urine, hypotension, rapid fall in Hb, positive direct Coombs | Immediate onset, evidence of intravascular hemolysis, complement‑mediated, not primarily respiratory. |

Acute hemolytic transfusion reaction: Fever, flank pain, ↓Hb, ↑LDH, ↓haptoglobin, positive DAT, hemoglobinuria, timing ≤ 4 h — Mild – symptoms controlled with fluids; Moderate – hypotension, renal impairment; Severe – shock, disseminated intravascular coagulation, death.

qs.q: Which of the following is a sign of an acute hemolytic transfusion reaction?
qs.e: Acute hemolytic transfusion reactions can manifest with a range of symptoms including fever, chills, hypotension (low blood pressure), back pain, and dark or red-colored urine (hemoglobinuria).
